PullRequest.Title: Agents window: stop sensitive edit locations ping-pong between windows
PullRequest.Body:

Fixes #341595. Builds on the idea in #343874 by @karthiknadig (stop re-asserting the value on every host update). This PR also changes what is written, so that one window's protections are never narrowed by another window's routine updates.

## Problem

Each window computes its sensitive edit locations from `chat.hookFilesLocations` / `chat.agentFilesLocations`, but the session holds one value. `BaseAgentHostSessionsProvider._seedRunningConfigFromState` called `_syncSensitiveEditLocations` on every session state update, and that wrote this window's exact list whenever the host's value differed. Two windows with different settings, for example the Agents window and an editor window with another profile or folder settings, overwrote each other forever. Each foreign write reached a window twice (as the `session/configChanged` action, then in the next state update), so one side wrote about twice as often.

Each write made the agent host broadcast config and meta changes to both windows. The session's pickers rebuilt continuously (mouse clicks were lost), and the agent host and both renderers stayed busy. The re-assert on every update came with #341342.

## Change

- `_syncSensitiveEditLocations` has two modes. `ensure` adds this window's missing locations to the host's value and never removes any. `replace` writes exactly this window's list.
- On host state updates and before a peer chat's first request, it uses `ensure`. On the first load of a running session and on a local settings change, it uses `replace`, so a window can still drop locations it no longer wants. Other windows add theirs back once.
- `AgentHostSessionHandler`: before a turn on an existing session, it works out the value from the session's live state right before sending. On this window's first turn, or once its own settings change, it sends exactly its own locations. Otherwise it sends the union of the host's value and this window's locations, and only if that differs. A new session still sends its own list.
- New `readChatSensitiveEditLocations` reads the untyped config value so it can be merged.

Windows that disagree now settle on the union of their locations. Protections can be over-applied, which means an extra confirmation, but another window's routine updates no longer narrow them. When a window deliberately replaces the value, the session protects only that window's locations for one round trip, until the other window adds its own back.

No protocol, setting or UI change.

## How to test

1. Open the Agents window and an editor window on the same machine. Give the editor window's folder `"chat.hookFilesLocations": { "other-hooks": true }` and enable `chat.viewSessions.sessionsList.enabled`.
2. Open the same Copilot CLI session in both windows.
3. The agent host log shows no repeating `session/configChanged`, and the mode/permissions picker opens with the mouse.

## Validation

- New tests: `two clients with different sensitive edit locations for one session settle on both of their locations` (localAgentHostSessionsProvider.test.ts), and in agentHostChatContribution.test.ts `handler keeps another client's hook locations when it sends a turn`, `handler restores its hook locations that another client dropped while the turn waited for authentication` and `handler sends exactly its hook locations once its settings change, then keeps another client's`. All fail without the product change and pass with it.
- `./scripts/test.sh --run` the local and remote agent host sessions provider, agentHostChatContribution, sessionPermissions and agentHostSchema test files: 2301 passing, 0 failing.
- `pnpm run typecheck-client` and `pnpm run oxlint` on the changed files: clean.
- Live, Code - OSS with both windows on one session, 60 s each, before → after: sensitive edit location writes 1699 + 849 per minute → about 10 per minute, only while toggling a setting, settling after each toggle; agent host CPU 57–96% → 0–3%; mode picker opened by a mouse click 0 of 3 → 3 of 3. Agents window JS heap after GC grew under 1 MB in both runs, so no per-event retention.

Validation ran on the main commit just before the `@microsoft/copilot-sdk` 2.0.1 bump, because that version wasn't installable locally yet. CI on this PR covers current main.

Written by GitHub Copilot on behalf of @sandy081

RegressionFixes.Mechanism: A config-state observer reasserted its own exact sensitive-location list whenever another window's list differed. For two clients with incompatible lists, every foreign state update produced another config dispatch, creating an idle feedback loop with repeated protocol broadcasts, config allocation/serialization/persistence, and picker DOM reconstruction. Local caching of computed locations did not suppress these differing-value writes.
RegressionFixes.Symptom: Strongly evidenced sustained agent-host/renderer work and repeated picker reconstruction while a shared session is idle, plus unbounded-in-time protocol and persistence operations until one client stops observing or the lists agree; no independent timing or CPU measurement was performed.
RegressionFixes.FixedBehavior: Routine session-state updates and existing peer-chat sends preserve the host's locations and add only missing local locations; equality suppresses writes once the clients reach their union. Exact replacement is reserved for initial config seeding or local setting changes. The turn handler likewise consults live state and avoids redundant writes on subsequent unchanged turns.
RegressionFixes.Evidence: The deleted base line 10208 calls _syncSensitiveEditLocations after seeding each changed SessionState config; the equal-config branch also calls it. Before the PR, desired was always computed.locations, and any differing host value triggered SessionConfigChanged. With two subscribed clients whose lists are A and B, each foreign config state therefore causes another exact-list write, preventing quiescence even while idle. _openSessionStateSubscription calls _applySessionStateUpdate on every state change, which calls _seedRunningConfigFromState. AgentHostProtocolClient.dispatchAction sends a dispatchAction notification; ProtocolServerHandler._broadcastAction sends the resulting envelope to relevant subscribed clients. _handleConfigChanged and _seedRunningConfigFromState fire picker events; AgentHostModePicker._updateTrigger clears and recreates label DOM. SessionFlagsContribution also queues config serialization and persistence for each config action. Added line 6369 merges the live host locations with local locations in ensure mode, and added lines 10204/10214 select ensure for subsequent state updates, so the union becomes equal and dispatch stops. The new two-client convergence test encodes this trigger. Blame resolves the old reassertion line to 0695d91131628a77143182333b5bf2a7a57245f4.

Scenarios.Scenario: Two windows observe the same running session with different sensitive-edit settings, including idle session/config updates.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: State delivery synchronously reaches _applySessionStateUpdate, _seedRunningConfigFromState, and _syncSensitiveEditLocations. Config events synchronously update visible pickers. Persistence is fire-and-forget rather than awaited by the renderer, but the former feedback loop continuously consumed host and renderer resources.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send one session/configChanged notification carrying the complete merged location array, then broadcast its action to relevant subscribed clients over the existing local/remote transport.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One outgoing dispatch per actual mismatch, with one action delivery per relevant subscribed client, commonly two windows. There is no per-location or per-folder RPC. Once both clients contain the union, routine updates dispatch zero location changes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same boundary existed, but each foreign list could provoke another exact-list counter-write indefinitely while idle; caching local locations did not prevent differing-value writes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Outgoing dispatch is not awaited, but resulting state/config events synchronously notify picker consumers. Transport windows and reconnect queues preserve existing delivery behavior.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Serialize persisted session config for each config action; sensitiveEditLocations itself is removed by omitTransientSessionConfigValues.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One serialization per config action, independent of the number of local folders. Quiescent shared settings now generate no further sensitive-location actions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Repeated for every feedback-loop config action even though sensitive locations are transient.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Executed in host action handling before the asynchronous persistence completes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Persist configValues through the central state database and flush its older-build metadata mirror where applicable.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One queued configValues update per config action, normally one central write plus applicable mirror/marker writes. This is per session, not per location; conflicts and mirror failures use existing retry behavior.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The idle loop continually enqueued these updates; the PR bounds them to actual changes and reconciliation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the renderer's awaited critical path. Updates are serialized by session key and can occupy the host's persistence queue.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Shared sessions multiplied by subscribed windows and state-event frequency; each array contains U unique paths after path-key deduplication and directory-flag merging. Two disagreeing windows are sufficient for the old loop.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Renderer state handling is synchronous; there is no new await or subprocess. Protocol broadcasts visit relevant clients. Persistence uses an existing SequencerByKey, allowing independent sessions to proceed but serializing each session's updates.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Provider local-location computation remains cached by session and workspace-folder string, invalidated on relevant settings changes and session removal. Ensure mode adds an O(U log U) merge and bounded temporary allocations per state update. Equality suppresses dispatch after convergence; malformed entries are filtered. No filesystem reads are used to compute locations.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: changed ensure/replace selection, dispatch suppression, observer call path, protocol broadcast, persistence, and picker DOM reconstruction are directly traced. The added two-client test encodes convergence.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: No independent profiling was performed. Number of shared sessions/windows and update frequency vary; no PR-description benchmark values were assumed.
Scenarios.Verdict: No introduced regression. This removes a concrete repeated-work feedback loop; its introducing commit was resolved and submitted through report_regression_fix.

Scenarios.Scenario: A user changes hook/agent location settings with multiple cached running sessions and drafts.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The existing configuration listener refreshes draft-derived values, clears the provider location cache, and synchronously visits cached sessions. Running sessions replace their list immediately; other observing windows subsequently ensure their own missing locations.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Dispatch an exact sensitive-location replacement for an eligible running session whose config differs.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one initial dispatch per eligible mismatching cached session, followed by finite union reconciliation across observing clients. Sessions lacking a connection or an advertised sensitive-location schema dispatch nothing. Folder/location count does not multiply RPC count.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Already cleared the cache, visited every cached session, and dispatched the same exact replacement. Subsequent foreign updates could previously restart indefinite reassertions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Dispatch occurs during the settings event; the listener does not await a host round trip.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Serialize and persist configValues for each dispatched replacement or reconciliation action.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Per dispatched session-level action, not per location. Per-session sequencing and mirror behavior are unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same persistence on initial replacements, with potentially unbounded subsequent feedback-loop writes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Asynchronous background persistence, not awaited by the settings listener.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: C cached sessions, of which E have running configs advertising the property; work computes locations across their folders only after cache invalidation. Typical arrays contain a small number of configured customization paths.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The renderer uses the existing synchronous loop and dispatches independently by session. No new global limiter or concurrency burst was added; host writes remain serialized per session.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Relevant settings changes explicitly clear the existing cache; recomputation is synchronous configuration lookup and path normalization. Exact replacement permits dropping old local locations, so deliberate local changes do not create an accumulating local-history cache.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed listener only makes its existing replacement semantics explicit; the collection loop and dispatch path predate the PR.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Eligible cached-session count and the number of other clients are workload-dependent; no timing measurements are available.
Scenarios.Verdict: No introduced fan-out regression. Existing session-level fan-out is preserved, while subsequent reconciliation no longer perpetually narrows other clients' values.

Scenarios.Scenario: Send a turn to an existing main or peer chat, including a host config change while authentication is pending.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Existing trust/model checks, pending creation/state hydration, authentication, and subscriptions complete before computing the changed security-config update and sending the turn. The new helper reads live subscribed state synchronously after authentication; it adds no await.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve authentication and forward a credential to the agent host when necessary.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: The production interactive resolver returns after processing its first protected resource. An unchanged successful credential requires zero new authenticate RPCs; same-key same-credential callers await one shared pending RPC.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same authentication was awaited here. Only location computation moved from before authentication to after it.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Authentication remains awaited before config dispatch and turn submission. Interactive sign-in may involve the existing authentication provider's network/UI flow.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Reuse or acquire session/chat subscriptions, then optionally dispatch one session-level config patch before the turn.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Warm subscriptions add no snapshot request; cold acquisition needs the existing session and selected-chat subscriptions. The location helper emits zero patches when equal, otherwise one patch containing the complete list. A committed peer's provider ensure can also patch missing values, but all chats share the backend-session key and local optimistic state.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Already acquired these subscriptions and dispatched config before turns. A nonempty local list previously produced a patch on every invocation, even when unchanged; peer ensure previously replaced foreign values.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cold hydration is an existing awaited prerequisite. Config dispatch preserves existing send ordering without a new awaited round trip.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Persist configValues when a session config patch is actually dispatched.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One persistence update per actual config action; zero sensitive-location-driven updates on an unchanged warm turn.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Redundant nonempty-list patches also triggered serialization and persistence.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Background host persistence rather than an awaited renderer prerequisite.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Turn frequency, number of session working roots, and U unique host/local location paths. State lookup does not fetch full history or perform per-root IPC.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Awaited prerequisites remain sequential in each invocation. Same-session chats share subscription references and the asserted-location entry; existing auth coalescing remains active. No new boundary concurrency was introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The new map stores one last-asserted local list per backend session, shared by its chats. Local locations are recomputed from in-memory settings each turn as before. Authentication caching keys resource/scopes/target plus credential identity; same-key in-flight forwarding coalesces. Live raw session state is an existing subscription read.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: both changed invocation sites, live-state helper, peer-send path, reference sharing, and credential forwarding/cache behavior were inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Cold hydration and interactive authentication duration depend on connection/provider behavior, but the diff does not increase those operations.
Scenarios.Verdict: No introduced latency or boundary-fan-out regression. Warm unchanged turns suppress redundant config writes, and foreign locations are preserved without another state fetch.

Scenarios.Scenario: Create a new backend session on its first request, including authentication failure/retry.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Compute initial locations, authenticate, prepare the session, resolve initial config if nonempty, create the session, and hydrate session/chat subscriptions before sending the turn. These awaited stages predate the PR.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve initial session config, create the backend session, and acquire session/chat snapshots using the existing connection.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Normally one conditional resolveSessionConfig RPC, one createSession RPC, and the existing session/chat subscriptions. Auth-required creation retains its existing single retry. Initial sensitive locations are included in the same creation payload, not sent through per-location calls.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Computed the same nonempty initial location config and used the same config-resolution/create/subscription flow.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing first-turn prerequisites; none are newly awaited or moved earlier by this diff.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Forward required credentials before session creation or on the existing auth-required retry.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Zero forwarding for a warm successful credential, otherwise one per changed credential/resource key with existing pending-request coalescing.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing awaited authentication; provider sign-in can require external interaction/network work.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: New-session creation count and configured working roots; location processing is in-memory and deduplicated by path.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Per invocation, creation prerequisites remain sequential. The PR neither launches additional sessions nor changes provider initialization or download concurrency.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The new helper remembers the local list under the requested backend-session key. _createAndSubscribe verifies that the returned URI matches that key. Session content ownership retains the entry until release, including normal failure/close cleanup; handler disposal clears the map.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for unchanged RPC counts and lifetime ownership: creation call flow, URI invariant, active-chat disposal, and map cleanup were read.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Backend initialization can be slow, but no independently introduced subprocess, filesystem scan, SDK download, or network operation was identified in the changed helpers.
Scenarios.Verdict: No introduced startup/eager-work regression. Initial payload behavior is preserved and location computation is deferred until the creation branch.

Scenarios.Scenario: Close chats or dispose the session handler/provider after using sensitive-location synchronization.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Chat release checks sibling/hydration holds, then deletes the new asserted-location entry and releases existing subscription references. Handler shutdown clears remaining entries after disposing active sessions.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Release existing refcounted session/default-chat/additional-chat subscriptions, unsubscribing on the final connection-level reference.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most the existing owned subscription releases per closed chat/session; sibling holds defer the shared releases. Deleting the new map entry adds no wire operation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Released the same references with the same sibling/hydration checks; the asserted-location map did not exist.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cleanup path, not a new prerequisite for turn submission.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Currently held backend sessions and their local configured-location lists, not completed turns or historical requests.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous ownership checks followed by existing reference disposal; no new delayed cleanup or disposal scheduling was added.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The new asserted map deletes on final session release and clears on handler disposal. Provider local-location entries are removed on session eviction/removal and cleared on settings changes. The map does not retain additional session state, transcript history, or DOM.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: insertion keys, final-release deletion, whole-handler clearing, provider eviction/removal, and existing hold checks were inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Open-session count and configured-array size vary; no evidence of substantial new retention beyond active ownership was found.
Scenarios.Verdict: No high-confidence unbounded-retention or cleanup regression.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance-review pass across all five changed files and every diff page; inventory and diff pagination ended at nextOffset 0. Traced shared-session convergence, settings-change fan-out, existing/peer turns, cold creation/authentication, and cache/subscription cleanup, including protocol, serialization, database/mirror, and rendering effects. No actionable high-confidence performance regression was introduced. Recorded one concrete feedback-loop regression fix with introducing commit 0695d91131628a77143182333b5bf2a7a57245f4 and its returned originPath. Static read-only review; no independent runtime measurements.
